content.comment_body: Ich habe ein [product_name]-PT100-Modul und diese schematische Darstellung. Auf meinem Bildschirm erscheint nur -50. Was mache ich falsch? Ich habe ein [product_name]-Systemmodul [article_no], aber ich habe keine analoge Anschlüsse definiert. Gibt es bereits Standard-Ports für analoge Eingänge?

To clarify in English: I have an [product_name]-PT100 module and a program like the one shown in my attachment. On my display, I only see -50. What am I missing? With my [product_name] basis module, I haven't reserved analog inputs—are standard ports assigned for these? If your 24VDC module is a [product_name], you can use 2 or 4 analog inputs if they're not in digital mode. Under File > Properties > Parameter, select either 2 or 4 analog inputs. If 2 are chosen, the first AM2 input is AI3; for 4 selected, it's AI5. Please provide the exact article number under the cursor key for certainty. Regards,

Sorry, I thought this forum was only for German. Here is a screenshot from my [product_name] software running in a Windows emulator. I believe I can only access the properties of the PT100 file, not those of the [product_name] [article_no] module. (The screenshot was originally .png but converted to .jpg).

I see what's wrong now. You are using a [product_name] [article_no] module in reality, correct? But in your software, you've selected the [product_name] [article_no] version, as indicated in the lower right corner of your screenshot. Use CTRL+H to choose the module that matches your hardware—always ensure you select the correct one. You can then choose between 2 or 4 analog inputs. Regards,

Yes, at the bottom of the screen was a picture of the [product_name] module. I switched it to the [article_no] version. Later I plan to use the analog inputs for RLV or other functions, but right now they're not in use. When I select analog input in the software, it always appears as AI. I changed the parameter to AI5 (since AI1-AI4 are on the head module [article_no]), but nothing changes; the output remains at -50.
Addendum: I use 12V for my [product_name] modules. Does that matter? I notice that most setups with the [product_name]-PT100 use 24V.

Hello, The [product_name]-PT100 module can operate on 12VDC, so something else may be wrong. Please check your wiring, as -50 indicates the minimum value for the [product_name] module. Refer to the manual for details: [url]. If wiring is correct, try all inputs—one should work. Regards,

The module showed a red indicator. I had a DM module between the [product_name] basis and the [product_name]-PT100 module, and it wasn't receiving power. After resolving the power issue, it works now.

analysis.insight_summary: The user consistently experienced issues connecting the [product_name]-PT100 module with the [product_name] basis, leading to wrong temperature readings. The underlying problem was due to hardware power connection, which prevented the module from working—seen as minimum value readings and a red indicator. The user also struggled with proper module selection in software, mapping inputs, and dealing with software in another language, all compounded by selecting the wrong module version.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects reliable module integration, accurate temperature measurement, simple hardware setup via software, and clear troubleshooting feedback. They anticipate support for both 12V and 24V DC operation and easy identification of configuration settings based on module versions.
